crystal: CO2 solid phase I (dry ice), the phase described by Trusler 2011 and Jaeger and Span 2012
source: P2 research-only fixture (batch 2026-09-24-coolprop-low-temperature) from open secondary values. Incomplete on purpose: no open source for the solid heat capacity between 189.78 K and the triple point, and none for the thermal expansion or compressibility, was available; the reference equations of state for solid CO2 (Trusler 2011, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40, 043105; Jaeger and Span 2012, J. Chem. Eng. Data 57, 590) are not available locally. Missing fields are left absent and the record refuses evaluation.

segments.source: Giauque and Egan 1937 (J. Chem. Phys. 5, 45) measured points as quoted by Wikipedia 'Carbon dioxide (data page)', retrieved 2026-09-24; linear interpolation between them is this record's assumption; the quoted 15.52 K point (2.534 J/(mol K)) is omitted because a straight line to it would misstate the low-temperature region

molar_volume.source: density 1562 kg/m3 of the solid at 1 atm and -78.5 C (Wikipedia 'Carbon dioxide' infobox, no primary citation, retrieved 2026-09-24) with the CoolProp molar mass 0.0440098 kg/mol; thermal_expansion_per_kelvin, isothermal_compressibility_per_pascal and the range are absent: not sourced

anchor.source: triple point 216.592 K and 0.51795 MPa: Span and Wagner 1996 (J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 25, 1509); fusion enthalpy 9.019 kJ/mol at the triple point: Air Liquide Gas Encyclopedia as quoted by Wikipedia 'Carbon dioxide (data page)', retrieved 2026-09-24 (secondary, estimated)

coverage.evidence: Incomplete: heat capacity ends at 189.78 K below the 216.592 K anchor; no thermal expansion, compressibility or volume range. Every evaluation is refused until Trusler 2011 or Jaeger and Span 2012 is acquired (P4).
